concept_weaknesses: The problem statement is too broad and does not describe the specific early-grade reading needs of the children served.
The target population is vague; specify grades K-3 and relevant characteristics such as low-income families and English language learners.
The activities are not defined. Describe the tutoring and family literacy activities, who will deliver them, and how many students and families will participate.
The outcome is broad and not measurable. Define reading outcomes and targets, using an appropriate assessment such as DIBELS where applicable.
The budget is marked TBD, and the proposal does not explain how the requested $75,000 would be used over 12 months.
concerns: The opportunity requires two letters of support; the listed evidence includes an MOU with two schools but does not establish that the required letters are available.
A logic model and five-page narrative are also required and are not listed as existing materials.
The organization reports pre/post DIBELS assessments for 241 of 312 tutored students; explain the assessment coverage and how results will inform the proposed project.
rationale: The organization meets all stated hard criteria: it is a 501(c)(3), its $850,000 budget is below the $3 million limit, and it serves Connecticut residents. Its K-3 literacy and family engagement work aligns with the stated priorities, and it has relevant program and assessment evidence. The concept is currently too vague to make a strong application; develop measurable outcomes, specific activities, and a complete budget before pursuing.
